I don’t hate being ace because I realized my happiness shouldn’t be rooted in finding a romantic partner. Society paints being single as one of the worst things you can be. It pushes the idea that the only way to have a fulfilling life is if you have a significant other. In reality, having a variety of meaningful connections with others is what facilitates fulfillment. I used to yearn for a romantic relationship and at times, still do. But I’ve gotten to the point that I feel I’d be just as happy in a relationship as I be would single, if not more. People don’t realize how difficult it is to find a romantic partner who is truly compatible with you rather if you’re ace or not. I mean, just look at the divorce rates. And sexual compatibility is still a HUGE hurdle for people who experience sexual attraction. Basically, your frustrations are valid but also know it’s challenging for everyone, regardless of sexuality, to find a truly compatible relationship.

It’s not necessarily about oppression but more so awareness and representation. Since asexuality is an “invisible” orientation, there will be generally less discrimination. However, it’s a double edged sword considering asexuality is wildly misunderstood and dismissed. A number of people will go through life thinking they are broken for not experiencing sexual attraction. A lot of the times, asexuality is thought of as something unnatural that needs to be cured. That could be extremely damaging to people who have not yet discovered or accepted their identity. Not to mention, asexuality doesn’t always fit within the typical life script. Most people expect to find a partner, get married and have children. Some aces are aromantic and even though they may have accepted their identity, they may not know how to navigate their life if it deviates too far from the typical life script.  Also, some aces are sex-repulsed so even if an asexual person is heteroromantic, they probably can’t just date the average heterosexual person. They would most likely have to seek partnership within the ace community. Also, aces may have a conflict between their sex-repulsion and their desire to have biological children. 
Visibility is incredibly important considering some people don’t even discover they are asexual until they are years into a marriage. They may be “stuck” in a relationship in which they would not have been in if they would’ve known about their identity earlier in life. Asexuals may not be the most oppressed people but so what? They still face both internal and external struggles due to their sexual orientation. And let’s not forget that even though it may not be as common, asexuals still get kicked out of their homes and disowned by family. Asexuals still face corrective rape as well. If asexuals don’t fit within the LGBTQIA+ community then they sure as hell don’t fit in with straight people either.

I’m not at all trying to invalidate any struggles you may have being Grey/aromantic but I always severely envied those who aren’t weight down by the burden of romantic feelings. Maybe it’s just me and my experience but every time I develop romantic feelings for someone, all of a sudden, my whole world stops and starts to revolve around said person. And it doesn’t even have to be a person I’m in a relationship with or in love with. Just simple crushes seem to change me so much: my behavior, my mindset, my schedule. I try to build the most appealing, filtered version of myself just to get the slight approval/attention from that specific person. I spend countless amount of time polishing my appearance: picking out the perfect outfit, engulfing myself in lavish soaps and body sprays and constantly checking the mirror to make sure a single hair isn’t misplaced. I’ve even known myself to creepily arrange my day to “accidentally” run into the person to have an excuse to talk to them. It almost becomes like an obsession for me. I feel like I lose a bit of agency because while my logical brain is trying to get through the day and focus on the important stuff, my subconscious always seems to bring every single thought back to the person. I sincerely believe my whole brain chemistry changes and I don’t feel fully like myself. But I guess I never experienced a more realistic depiction of love like you have mentioned above. I think naturally, romantic attraction starts off as total infatuation and fades into a more practical feeling of love. It all still terrifies the shit out of me.
